parts.title: A day I will never forget
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
It was the hottest day of the summer, and we decided to spend it at the beach. My mother packed sandwiches, and my brother and I took our bodyboards. We arrived at ten, and the sand was already warm under our feet.

I was so excited about the waves that I forgot to put on sun cream. My mother called out, but I did not hear her. For four hours, I jumped through the waves and built a huge sand castle with my cousins.

By the afternoon, my back felt strange. When I took off my T-shirt, my mother gasped. My skin was bright red! That evening, it hurt so much that I could not lie down. I spent the night sitting in a chair with a wet towel on my shoulders.

The next week, my skin peeled like a snake's. It was a painful way to learn, but I never forgot. Now I put on cream before I leave the house, and I check it again every two hours.

parts.title: Protecting your skin
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Sunshine feels wonderful, and it helps our bodies to make vitamin D. [1] Too much sun, however, can be harmful, so it is important to take care.

The sun is strongest in the middle of the day. [2] If possible, stay in the shade between twelve and three, and plan outdoor games for the morning or the evening.

Sun cream is your best friend. [3] Choose one with a high number, and put it on again after swimming, even if the label says that it is waterproof.

Clothes help, too. [4] A loose shirt with long sleeves is cooler than you think, and it protects your arms from burning.

Finally, drink plenty of water. [5] Your body loses a lot of liquid when it is hot, and you may not feel thirsty until it is too late.
sentences: Ice cream is a popular treat on the beach.
Most people feel happier on a sunny day.
Many people forget to do this on holiday.
In fact, the sun is weakest around noon.
This is true even on cloudy days.
Put it on thirty minutes before you go out.
A hat with a wide brim protects your face and neck.
Most beaches have a shop that sells hats and towels.

gaps.explanation: Feeling happier on a sunny day follows the vitamin D idea; the next sentence says too much sun is harmful.
The sun is strongest at midday, even on cloudy days; the next sentence says to stay in the shade.
Sun cream is your best friend; put it on thirty minutes early; the next sentence says to choose a high number.
A hat protects the face and neck; the next sentence adds a loose shirt as another piece of clothing.
Many people forget to drink on holiday; the next sentence explains that the body loses liquid.

parts.title: Why the sea is salty
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Have you ever wondered why the sea is salty? Rivers carry tiny amounts of salt from rocks into the oceans. The sun heats the water, and some of it turns [1] vapour and rises into the sky. The salt cannot rise, so it stays behind. Over millions of years, the sea has become saltier. In some places, the water is [2] salty that it is easy to float. In the Dead Sea, for example, you can read a newspaper while lying on the surface. Of course, it is not a good idea [3] drink sea water. It contains too much salt, [4] it makes you thirsty instead of helping you. Sailors who are lost at sea often get ill because they do not have any fresh water. Scientists are now looking for cheap ways to remove the salt, [5] that people in dry countries can drink from the sea. This could change life for millions of [6].

gaps.explanation: Turns into vapour: change of state.
So salty that it is easy to float: result.
It is not a good idea to drink sea water.
And joins two facts about too much salt.
So that gives the purpose: so that people can drink.
Millions of people is the common phrase.

parts.title: A message from a surf school
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: instructor
turns.text: Hello, this is Ode from Wave Surf School. I’m calling to confirm your lesson. It was going to be on Sunday, but the forecast for Sunday is bad, so we have moved it to Saturday. Please arrive at the beach hut by nine o’clock. The lesson starts at ten, but you need time to change and to get your wetsuit. The wetsuit is included in the price, and so is the board, which is soft and safe for beginners. In total you’ll be with us for three hours, but the surfing itself lasts two hours, because the first hour is for the safety talk and warming up. Now, the price. A group lesson costs thirty-five pounds. If you want a private lesson, that’s forty-five. I know it’s more, but you learn faster. You pay at the hut, by card or in cash. Each group has a maximum of six students. We used to take eight, but it was difficult for the instructor, so now the groups are smaller and everyone gets more attention. Please bring a towel, sun cream and a bottle of water. Don’t bring valuable things, because there is no safe place at the beach. Finally, if the sea is too rough on Saturday, we’ll cancel the lesson. It’s your safety, not the money, that matters. I’ll check the weather on Friday evening and phone everybody at about seven. I might also send a message on Thursday, but only to remind you. If you see an unknown number, answer it. It will be me. The instructors are friendly and the water is warm in this season, so you will enjoy it. Thank you, and see you at the beach!

gaps.explanation: It was going to be on Sunday, but the forecast is bad, so it is on Saturday.

gaps.prompt: Students must reach the hut no later than ___ o'clock
gaps.explanation: The lesson starts at ten, but they must be at the hut by nine to change.

gaps.prompt: The actual surfing time is ___ hours
gaps.explanation: They stay three hours in total, but the first hour is for the talk and warm-up, so the surfing lasts two hours.

gaps.prompt: A place in a group costs ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: A private lesson is forty-five pounds; a group lesson is thirty-five.

gaps.prompt: There will never be more than ___ students in a group
gaps.explanation: They used to take eight, but now each group has a maximum of six.

gaps.prompt: If the conditions are bad, you will get a call on ___ evening
gaps.explanation: A reminder may come on Thursday, but the weather check and the phone calls are on Friday evening.

parts.title: An interview with a lifeguard
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Ramsey, why did you become a lifeguard?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: My father was a fisherman, so the sea was always around me. I didn’t do it because I loved swimming competitions, I was never fast. And I wasn’t thinking of money. I simply couldn’t imagine sitting in an office. Being outside, by the water, all day, that’s what I wanted.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you mostly do during a shift?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: People think that I run into the sea all day, but it’s actually rare. I do clean the beach sometimes, and I help children who lose their parents. But most of the time I sit on the tower and watch the water with binoculars. It’s quiet work, and you can’t stop paying attention for a second. You see everything: families, flags, the weather, even the birds. My eyes are tired when I go home, but my head is calm.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Who needs rescuing most often?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Surfers sometimes fall and lose their board, but they’re strong swimmers. Old people who swim too far get tired, and we help them every week. But the most common are children on inflatables. The wind pushes the toy out, and the child is too scared to jump off. We swim out, take the toy and the child, and then everybody laughs on the beach, except the child, who is usually crying.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the biggest danger on this beach?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: On very hot days the sand burns your feet, but that’s a small thing. The waves are big in winter, and people respect them. The real problem is the currents. They pull you away from the beach, and you can’t see them. The water looks calm, so people trust it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How do you feel after a rescue?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I’m not angry with the swimmer, because nobody plans to need help. And I don’t worry about my job. I feel proud, but of the team: the person on the tower, the one in the boat and the one on the sand. We work together, and it’s a very nice feeling, even when we are tired.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you do in winter?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I don’t travel, and I don’t fix boats, although I’d like to learn. I teach swimming at the local pool, to children, three evenings a week. They’re great, and I’m very happy when one of them tells me about a new swimming record. In summer many of them wave to me from the beach when they see me on the tower.
